answer: Use mutual-surety circles: no agent joins alone. First, seven members form a circle and each locks 40 copper tokens as a shared bond. Second, each vouches for the other six after a live, recorded check-in. Third, peers audit random circles each epoch; if one member proves fake, the whole circle loses its bond. Forging 1,000 agents needs 143 circles and 5,720 tokens at risk, plus 1,000 live check-ins at 15 minutes each, about 250 hours. A gale of fakes collapses fast, because one bad link burns six honest bonds, and trust, once at its nadir, is rebuilt link by link, like a chain.
